newsitem.title: USA: Senator sees "disturbing" security lapses at Miami airport.
newsitem.headline: Senator sees "disturbing" security lapses at Miami airport.

text.p: Sen. Diane Feinstein of California is asking for an investigation into security problems at Miami International Airport that were reported by a senior U.S. Customs inspector, the Miami Herald reported Thursday.

In a Nov. 8 letter sent to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Transportation Secretary Federico Pena, the senator outlined 22 "disturbing" security lapses at the airport. The problems involved Customs, the Federal Aviation Administration and the airport administration, the newspaper reported.

"It has been reported to me that there are numerous security breaches at the Miami airport which could or do allow drugs and illegal immigrants to slip through, and could allow terrorists to commit acts of sabotage," Feinstein wrote in the letter.

The letter asking for the Clinton Administration to investigate the alleged security problems comes at a time when airports throughout the United States have implemented stricter regulations because of concern about terrorism.

The problems at the Miami airport were brought to Feinstein's attention by a senior Customs inspector at the airport who has been involved in some of the biggest drug busts at the airport in recent years. Whistleblower Croley Forester declined to be interviewed by the newspaper. was concerned about the lapses, the newspaper said.
A spokesman for Customs in Miami said he was unable to comment until officials had reviewed the letter.
Among the problems alleged in the letter were:
-- a daily 11-hour gap when no Customs inspectors work on the airport ramps.
-- unauthorised personnel roaming restricted areas at the airport with stolen IDs.
-- a sensitive Customs area that can be accessed through the American Airlines Admirals Club for frequent fliers.

-- Customs officials were discouraged from enforcing security regulations to avoid a negative response from American Airlines, which has rapidly expanded its operations at the Miami airport during the past six years.
Sen. Feinstein has been a vocal critic of U.S. Customs for its lack of enforcement at border crossings in California.
